title: The load planner, step by step

steps.title: Read the file
steps.note: Architecture, block_count and tensor sizes come from the GGUF itself, never from its name.

steps.title: Measure the machine
steps.note: Free VRAM and RAM through NVML, with nvidia-smi as fallback. A value it cannot measure stays null rather than becoming an estimate.

steps.title: Detect the platform
steps.note: Native Linux, WSL2 or a given driver each impose different constraints, and WSL2 is where the wrong guess costs the most.

steps.title: Produce a plan
steps.note: GPU layers, context, batch, KV cache type and environment, each value carrying the reason it was chosen.

steps.title: Degrade, never escalate
steps.note: After a failed load it lowers the plan and inherits the constraint. The v1 raised the context after each failure until the machine gave up.
